title: The Museum Heist
briefing_md:
On Monday at 9 AM, curator Fatima Sheikh opened the City Heritage Museum and found the glass case of the Maharani's Emerald Necklace perfectly intact, with a necklace inside. But tests proved it was a fake.

No alarm rang, no glass broke, and the case was locked. On Sunday evening the museum had hosted Heritage Night, a party for donors.

Three people are being talked about:
• Joseph Pinto, 47, the night guard. He says he did his rounds and saw nothing.
• Rekha Bhandari, 42, a jewellery designer (“RB Designs”) and donor guest. She says she admired the necklace but never touched it.
• Ramesh Bose, 50, the caterer for Heritage Night. He says he never left the banquet hall.

Most people suspect the night guard. When and how did the real necklace vanish, and who took it?

clue.label: The necklace
clue.title: The fake and the original
clue.text:
• The necklace in the case is lighter than the original. Its clasp is plain and modern.
• The catalogue photo of the original shows a clasp engraved with a small lion.
• The glass case is unbroken and locked.

questions.question: What kind of theft was this?
options: A smash-and-grab in the middle of the night
The real necklace was swapped for a copy
The necklace was lost during cleaning
Nothing was actually stolen

clue.label: Sketchbook
clue.title: A young visitor's drawing
clue.text:
A 10-year-old visitor drew the necklace on Saturday at 4 PM.
His sketch clearly shows the little lion on the clasp.

questions.question: What does the sketch tell us?
options: The swap happened before Saturday
The boy drew the fake necklace
The boy should be treated as a suspect
The real one was still there on Saturday

clue.label: Cleaner's log
clue.title: Sunday morning
clue.text:
Sunday 8 AM — Imran cleaned the glass of the case.
He wrote: “Necklace sparkling nicely. The little lion is shining.”

questions.question: What does this narrow down?
options: The swap happened after Sunday 8 AM
The swap happened on Saturday night
Imran swapped the necklace while cleaning
The necklace was a fake from the start

clue.label: Alarm and CCTV
clue.title: Sunday night
clue.text:
• No alarm rang.
• The gallery camera was off from 2 AM to 3 AM for routine maintenance.
• The case's lock sensor shows the case was not opened at any time that night.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the night?
options: The thief opened the case between 2 AM and 3 AM
The thief cut the alarm wires before midnight
The case stayed shut all night
The guard switched the camera off on purpose

clue.label: Key box
clue.title: When the case was opened
clue.text:
The case key stays in the curator's locked key box.
On Sunday the case was opened only once: at 7:15 PM, by the curator, to show the necklace to guests at Heritage Night (6 PM to 9 PM).

questions.question: When could the swap have happened?
options: On Monday morning at 9 AM
During the cleaning at 8 AM
On Saturday afternoon at 4 PM
While the case was open on Sunday evening

clue.label: Initials
clue.title: A mark on the fake
clue.text:
Tiny initials are stamped on the hinge of the fake: “R.B.”

Two of the people being talked about have these initials: Rekha Bhandari and Ramesh Bose.

questions.question: What can we say so far?
options: It proves that Rekha made and swapped it
It proves that Ramesh made and swapped it
It points to an R.B., but which one could reach it?
The initials are only the shop's price code

clue.label: Guest list
clue.title: Wristbands at Heritage Night
clue.text:
• Blue wristband: donors, allowed into the gallery. Rekha had a blue wristband.
• Green wristband: caterers, banquet hall only. Ramesh had a green wristband.
• A waiter: “The caterers stayed in the banquet hall. The corridor to the gallery needs a blue wristband.”

questions.question: Could Ramesh have reached the necklace?
options: Yes, caterers were allowed everywhere
No, he could not enter the gallery
Yes, he had the curator's key
Yes, but only after 9 PM

clue.label: The guard
clue.title: Joseph Pinto
clue.text:
• In his locker: a loan recovery letter. He owes money.
• Patrol sheet: Joseph was at the main gate from 7 PM to 9 PM, signed by two colleagues.

questions.question: What does this tell us about Joseph?
options: He owes money, but he was at the gate
He needed money, so he must have done it
He was in the gallery at 7:15 PM
He made the fake necklace himself

twist_md: New evidence has come in: statements from the curator and from another guest who was in the gallery.

clue.label: Curator's statement
clue.title: Fatima Sheikh
clue.text: “At 7:15 I unlocked the case so that Rekha and Mr. Anil could see the necklace up close. At 7:20 I stepped out for a phone call and was gone about five minutes. I relocked the case at 7:25.”

twist_questions.question: When was the open case not watched by the curator?
options: From 6:00 PM to 7:15 PM
From 7:25 PM to 9:00 PM
From 7:20 PM to 7:25 PM
From 2:00 AM to 3:00 AM

clue.label: Guest's statement
clue.title: Mr. Anil Chopra, donor, 78
clue.text:
Mr. Anil has poor eyesight.

“Rekha held the necklace while Fatima was out. She turned her back to me.”

twist_questions.question: What most likely happened in those five minutes?
options: Rekha swapped it for a copy she had made
Mr. Anil took the necklace home with him
The curator hid the necklace in her office
Rekha only admired it, just as she said

clue.label: Guest's statement
clue.title: Later that evening
clue.text:
Mr. Anil: “Later that evening Rekha told me her studio is nearly bankrupt.”

The necklace is worth crores.

twist_questions.question: What was the motive?
options: Revenge on the curator
To embarrass the museum
A dare from a friend
Money to save her studio

answer.explanation: Rekha Bhandari swapped the real necklace for a replica she had made (stamped R.B.) on Sunday evening, between 7:20 and 7:25 PM, while the curator was out on a phone call. She held the necklace with her back to Mr. Anil, who has poor eyesight. The boy's Saturday sketch and the cleaner's Sunday 8 AM log show the real necklace, with its lion clasp, was there until Sunday. The case was not opened at night, so the camera gap is irrelevant. Ramesh Bose shares the initials but had a green wristband and could not enter the gallery. Joseph owes money but was at the main gate from 7 to 9 PM. Rekha's studio was nearly bankrupt.
